chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Karim from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked him: When a man performs Hajj on behalf of his brother, or his father, or any other person, is it appropriate for him to recite something? He said: 'Yes. After he enters the state of Ihram, he should say: O God, grant reward to so-and-so for the hardship, strain, affliction, or hunger that befalls me during this journey, and grant me reward for my performing the Hajj on his behalf.'

key_terms.فُلاَنًا: so-and-so (the person on whose behalf the act is done)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for someone performing Hajj on behalf of another person?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific supplication recited by the *muqaddam* (representative) after entering Ihram, emphasizing the transfer of reward for physical hardships to the principal. It highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of Hajj as a vicarious act where the agent's endurance of trials serves as a means of spiritual merit for the one who is unable to perform it personally. The text underscores the communal and intercessory nature of worship in Shia jurisprudence, linking personal sacrifice to the fulfillment of another's religious duty.
